mechanisms.name: Keep what must not be obtained together in different places
mechanisms.description: Parts that give access or trust only in combination (strip and bag, signers, seed and passphrase, device and PIN) are kept in different places, so that no single place, person or event yields all of them.

mechanisms.name: Strip stored apart from the bag
mechanisms.description: The strip is kept in a different place than the bag it belongs to.

mechanisms.name: Signers stored in different places
mechanisms.description: The devices and backups of the signers of one policy are kept in different locations and are reachable by different people.

mechanisms.name: Secrets stored apart from what they unlock
mechanisms.description: A passphrase is kept apart from its seed, and a PIN or password apart from the device or item it protects.

mechanisms.name: Require several independent parts to act
mechanisms.description: Access or spending needs more than one independent part (several signers, a seed plus a passphrase), so that compromising one part is not enough; this only holds as long as the parts are not obtained together.

mechanisms.name: Several signers required
mechanisms.description: Every spending policy that can be used at once needs at least two signers.

mechanisms.name: Seed protected by a passphrase
mechanisms.description: The seed alone does not open the wallet; a passphrase that is kept separately is needed as well.

mechanisms.name: Device locked by a PIN
mechanisms.description: The signing device needs a PIN to unlock, so holding the device alone is not enough to use the seed on it.

mechanisms.name: Keep more than one copy, signer or path
mechanisms.description: One loss, failure or absence does not block access or recovery, because there is another copy, signer or path.

mechanisms.name: Redundant backups in different locations
mechanisms.description: Every secret or item that must survive has more than one backup copy, in different locations.

mechanisms.name: More signers than the threshold
mechanisms.description: A policy has more signers than its threshold, so some signers can fail or be unavailable.

mechanisms.name: Fallback spending policy
mechanisms.description: A delayed policy lets other signers take over if the usual ones are gone.

mechanisms.name: Check with a second, independent source before trusting
mechanisms.description: Firmware, software, addresses, transactions and restored secrets are verified against a source that does not share the failure of the thing being checked.

mechanisms.name: Verify firmware before installing
mechanisms.description: Check the signature or hash of every firmware that is installed, and when the device is set up.

mechanisms.name: Verify the coordinator download
mechanisms.description: Check the signature of the coordinator software before installing it.

mechanisms.name: Verify addresses on a device screen
mechanisms.description: Compare every send, receive and change address, and the receive address of every large incoming payment, with the screen of a signing device before relying on it.
mechanisms.signal: The address on the device screen differs from the one in the coordinator.

mechanisms.name: Check each transaction on several devices
mechanisms.description: Verify receiver, amount and change on the screens of the signing devices, ideally of different makes, before signing.
mechanisms.signal: Devices or the coordinator show a different receiver, amount or change.
mechanisms.caveat: Works only across devices that do not share a flaw (same model, same vendor).

mechanisms.name: Anti-phishing words
mechanisms.description: The device shows words that are derived from its seed; compare them with the ones noted at setup.
mechanisms.signal: The words differ from the ones noted at setup.

mechanisms.name: Reset and re-initialise a device from the backup
mechanisms.description: After the first receive transaction, wipe the device and restore the seed from its backup; the fingerprint must be the same.
mechanisms.signal: The restored seed gives a different fingerprint, or the backup is rejected.

mechanisms.name: Regularly check that every part of the setup is present, intact and usable
mechanisms.description: Atomic checks of single entities are combined into checks of parts of the setup and finally of the whole setup; the refining mechanisms state which check runs how often.

mechanisms.name: Tamper-evident bag opened
mechanisms.description: Look at the seal of the bag whenever the place is visited.
mechanisms.signal: The seal is broken or shows signs of opening.
mechanisms.caveat: Does not detect T-BAG-BYPASSED by definition.

mechanisms.name: Tamper-evident bag: serial does not match
mechanisms.description: Compare the serial on the bag with the strip that is kept elsewhere.
mechanisms.signal: The serial on the bag differs from the strip.
mechanisms.caveat: Does not help against T-STRIP-SWAPPED-WITH-BAG; strip and bag must not be reachable together.

mechanisms.name: Inspect the location
mechanisms.description: Visit the place and look for damage, intrusion, digging or changes.
mechanisms.signal: Damage, signs of entry, changed surroundings or lost access.

mechanisms.name: Check the cloud account
mechanisms.description: Log in, check the login history and that the files are still there.
mechanisms.signal: Unknown logins, missing files or a locked account.

mechanisms.name: Power on and check the devices
mechanisms.description: Unlock each device, check display, buttons, connectors, battery and firmware state.
mechanisms.signal: The device does not start, the PIN is not accepted, the battery is empty or the screen shows an error.

mechanisms.name: Verify the backups
mechanisms.description: Read each backup and compare it with another copy or with the device.
mechanisms.signal: The copy is missing, unreadable or differs from the other copies.

mechanisms.name: Test transaction
mechanisms.description: Receive a small amount and send it on with the real devices and coordinator.
mechanisms.signal: A step of the receive or send fails, or the addresses and fingerprints differ from expectation.

mechanisms.name: Contact the people involved
mechanisms.description: Call or meet every owner, heir and trustee: are they reachable, do they know their role and still agree to it.
mechanisms.signal: A person cannot be reached or no longer knows or agrees to their role.

mechanisms.name: Compare the plan with the setup
mechanisms.description: Check that the plan matches the actual setup and that its copies are where the plan says.
mechanisms.signal: The plan differs from the setup, or a copy is missing.

mechanisms.name: Recovery drill
mechanisms.description: Let heirs and trustees walk through the plan without moving funds, and fix what they stumble over.
mechanisms.signal: Helpers get stuck, or the instructions are wrong or missing.

mechanisms.name: Watch for signs of an incident
mechanisms.description: Movements and events are observed continuously or when they happen, so that an incident shows up without waiting for the next health check.

mechanisms.name: Watch the balance
mechanisms.description: A watch-only coordinator or alert service reports every movement of the wallet.
mechanisms.signal: A spend that the owners did not make.
mechanisms.caveat: Detection only matters if the owners can still respond (sweep, or satisfy a policy that beats the attacker).

mechanisms.name: Tripwire funds move
mechanisms.description: A wallet with a small amount whose secrets are kept next to the secrets of the real wallets; anyone who finds them will spend from it first.

weakened_when.reason: the attacker knows a descriptor that contains the tripwire key, so he sees the bigger wallet behind it and is unlikely to touch the tripwire

mechanisms.caveat: Triggers only if the attacker reaches the tripwire secrets together with the real ones; the response is to sweep the real wallets (R-SWEEP-WALLET).

mechanisms.name: Check that the transaction confirms
mechanisms.description: After broadcasting, follow the transaction until it is confirmed.
mechanisms.signal: The transaction stays unconfirmed, for example because the fee is too low.

mechanisms.name: Renew or refresh what ages or expires before it fails
mechanisms.description: Things with a limited life (media, seals, timelocks, the plan) are renewed on a schedule instead of waiting for them to fail.

mechanisms.name: Refresh the timelock
mechanisms.description: Move the coins with the immediate policy before the delay of the recovery paths expires.

mechanisms.name: Renew backups periodically
mechanisms.description: Copy the item to a new medium before the old one has degraded.

mechanisms.name: Reseal bags periodically
mechanisms.description: Replace the bag before its adhesive degrades.

mechanisms.name: Review and update the plan
mechanisms.description: Go through the plan, correct what changed and re-store its copies.

mechanisms.name: Device that shows and verifies the transaction
mechanisms.description: The signing device displays receiver, amount and change itself; a device that can only sign blind is not used.

mechanisms.name: Limited PIN attempts
mechanisms.description: The device allows only a maximum number of wrong PIN attempts before it wipes or bricks itself, so the PIN cannot be brute-forced.
mechanisms.caveat: The same limit makes T-DEV-WIPED-BY-ATTEMPTS possible.

mechanisms.name: Descriptor registered on the signing devices
mechanisms.description: Every signing device of a multisig or custom wallet has the wallet descriptor registered, so it can check the multisig policy and the change before it signs. Done once when the wallet is set up (R-REGISTER-DESCRIPTOR); the setup says it with `stores_descriptors`, and the device catalog must say that the device registers descriptors (unknown counts as no).

mechanisms.name: Load the descriptor from the stored copy for every signing
mechanisms.description: A device that does not keep a registered descriptor is given the wallet descriptor from the owner's own copy before each signing and the owner confirms it on the device screen. It only works if the copy is kept where the device is, so it can be loaded when needed.

mechanisms.name: Setup test with every signer
mechanisms.description: Before real funds are used, the wallet is tested from end to end: a small amount is received and sent on, in as many rounds with different groups of signers that every signer takes part at least once. A wrong or incomplete descriptor, a missing key or a wrong threshold fails here and is corrected before it matters.

mechanisms.name: Spending needs a journey
mechanisms.description: The least time a person needs to bring together a group of signers that can spend at once, starting at the most favourable place, is long enough that a short phase of bad judgement is over before they get there. The setup says the travel times between the places.

mechanisms.name: Private workspace for secrets
mechanisms.description: Whenever a secret is created or entered, the place is first made free of observers and sensors.

mechanisms.name: Metal backup
mechanisms.description: The item is stamped or engraved in steel, titanium or similar instead of being written on paper.
mechanisms.caveat: Fire, water, crush and corrosion resistance of the product is already taken into account by the location threats through the catalogue.

mechanisms.name: Device bought directly from the vendor
mechanisms.description: The device reaches the owner without a reseller or a mail hop that is not under the vendor's control.

mechanisms.name: Educate the people involved
mechanisms.description: Teach everyone with access or knowledge about the risks and the rules of the setup.

mechanisms.name: Run your own node
mechanisms.description: The coordinator queries a node you operate, so no third party learns xpubs, addresses or balances.
mechanisms.caveat: The node is not modelled as an entity.
